name: Byung-Cheol Min
title: Professor
department: Computer Science and Intelligent Systems Engineering; SMART Lab
fitReason: Strong overlap with CS methods for embodied AI: human-aware learning, language-based task planning, uncertainty estimation, and actual robot execution. The September 2026 touch-based manipulation study offers a concrete software/evaluation direction; the lab's human-preference work broadens HRI fit.

physicalEvidence.summary: The September 24, 2026 primary preprint Audit Before You Commit identifies both authors with IU SMART Lab. Section V-D describes a physical Hiwonder JetRover five-DOF arm using a touch switch to locate a rigid pocket and perform one-shot insertion. The experiment runs particle-based belief updating and scenario-based action selection over 118 episodes. The separate April 2026 SafeGate LLM-robot paper still identifies the team with Purdue, so its hardware is not attributed to IU.

shortVisit.summary: The current SMART Lab opportunities page explicitly includes a Collaborators, Postdocs and Visiting Researchers section inviting contact, updated to Indiana University and minb@iu.edu despite a stale Purdue heading. The lab also reports a graduate visiting student arriving in August 2026; that precedent adds context but is not an open summer position. No visit duration, external master's eligibility or 2027 slot is promised.

scoreReasons.fit: strong human-aware robot learning, language planning and probabilistic methods.

The visitor invitation is broad and duration-unspecified. An approximately eight-week external master's research plan, supervision and funding require approval.

Existing IU institutional notes describe a conditional foreign-degree J-1 Student Intern route, at least 32 hours per week and advance departmental processing. This does not establish personal-funding acceptability or category approval for graduate visitors.

The September study is a preprint submitted for possible publication. Its project page labels ICRA 2027, but acceptance is not established. Its offline audit is not a deployment-wide safety guarantee.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
